problem:
The function ${y}_{0}(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x$ is a particular solution of the Riccati differential equation

$$
{y}^{′}=4{y}^{2}-(8\operatorname{sin}⁡x+4)y+(4{sin}^{2}⁡x+4\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x).
$$

Express this equation in the Bernoulli form

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+P(x)z=Q(x){z}^{n}
$$

and state the functions $P(x)$ and $Q(x),$ and the value of $n.$

$P(x)=$
{{field-1}}
$,\,Q(x)=$
{{field-2}}
$,\,n=$
{{field-3}}
worked_solution:
A Riccati differential equation has the form

$$
{y}^{′}=a(x){y}^{2}+b(x)y+c(x).
$$

To reduce the given Riccati equation to a Bernoulli equation, we use the substitution

$$
y(x)=z(x)+{y}_{0}(x),
$$

where ${y}_{0}(x)$ is a known particular solution.
Differentiating gives

$$
{y}^{′}(x)={z}^{′}(x)+{y}_{0}^{′}(x).
$$

In our case, ${y}_{0}(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$ Since ${y}_{0}^{′}(x)=\operatorname{cos}⁡x$, we have

$$
y=z+\operatorname{sin}⁡x\,⇒\,{y}^{′}={z}^{′}+\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

Let's substitute these expressions into our Riccati equation:

$$
{z}^{′}+\operatorname{cos}⁡x=4(z+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{2}-(8\operatorname{sin}⁡x+4)(z+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)+(4{sin}^{2}⁡x+4\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x).
$$

Now, we expand the right-hand side, and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}^{′}+\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =4(z+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)^{2}-(8\operatorname{sin}⁡x+4)(z+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)+(4{sin}^{2}⁡x+4\operatorname{sin}⁡x+\operatorname{cos}⁡x) \\ {z}^{′}+\operatorname{cos}⁡x & =4{z}^{2}-4z+\operatorname{cos}⁡x \\ {z}^{′}+4z & =4{z}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

This is a Bernoulli equation of the form

$$
\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}x}+P(x)z=Q(x){z}^{n}
$$

where

$$
P(x)=4,\,Q(x)=4,\,n=2.
$$
